messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: .Rcache directory
parts:
Hi,

I am working on a server and the working directory is not in my home
directory but in a shared directory among users. I just got the
following error
[2007-12-10 22:14:36] Exception: Could not create cache directory:
~/.Rcache/aroma.affymetrix/HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl47,G-Affy,monocell

This is probably because I don't have a home directory on this server
(don't know why, actually, bit odd that). But this made me realize that
the .Rcache will be saved on every user's home directory separately.
Does this really make sense when there are multiple users using the same
data? And can I change this location to a folder in the working
directory where all the aroma.affymetrix folders are since I don't have
a home directory ('~/' doesn't work)?

Thanks,
Elizabeth

On 10/12/2007, Elizabeth Purdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I am working on a server and the working directory is not in my home
> directory but in a shared directory among users. I just got the
> following error
> [2007-12-10 22:14:36] Exception: Could not create cache directory:
> ~/.Rcache/aroma.affymetrix/HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl47,G-Affy,monocell
>
> This is probably because I don't have a home directory on this server
> (don't know why, actually, bit odd that). But this made me realize that
> the .Rcache will be saved on every user's home directory separately.
> Does this really make sense when there are multiple users using the same
> data? And can I change this location to a folder in the working
> directory where all the aroma.affymetrix folders are since I don't have
> a home directory ('~/' doesn't work)?

See the FAQ, but also the Page 'Caching of computational expensive tasks':

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/frequently-asked-questions

If you want everyone to share the same file cache, you might want to
use the option to specify the path via a system environment variable
and have the sysadm set for everyone. You probably don't want to use
/tmp/ (supposedly erased frequently and at reboot) but rather
/var/tmp/, cf.

http://www.comptechdoc.org/os/linux/usersguide/linux_ugfilestruct.html

/Henrik

>
> Thanks,
> Elizabeth
